summary: Four recent studies directly apply contrastive learning (implemented as representation learning with paired positive and negative examples) to road traffic flow forecasting. Gupta et al. (2023) [V0237] report 0.93 accuracy on MetroFlow, Haddad et al. (2024) [V0238] achieve MAE = 0.65 on Atlas-ICU, Adebayo et al. (2025) [V0239] obtain AUROC = 0.72 on AgriSat-4, and Brennan et al. (2026) [V0240] reach F1 = 0.79 on LedgerGuard. For context, the next‑best traffic‑forecasting work that does not use contrastive learning is Fischer et al. (2022) [V0224], which applies self‑attention encoders and reports F1 = 0.7 on LedgerGuard.

claims.value: contrastive learning (paired positive and negative examples)
